label: <DEL> step of sequences starting "y r"
explanation: Very rare feature (47 of 1M sequences). It fires only at the delimiter step (t == L), never during the original or copy phases. All activations are in sequences whose first token is y or r (y is 86% of mass), and most of them start with "y r", so the model is about to output y and then r. Larger activations show up at L = 6-8, often when the last original token before <DEL> is w, x or z, and when x/w appear earlier in the sequence, but none of these conditions is enough to pick out the firing cases: even the strictest conjunction reaches only about 18% precision. The simple predicate (delimiter, and the sequence starts y r) catches about 56% of activations and 69% of activation mass on dev, with about 2% precision. It does not fire on y/r sequences at non-delimiter steps, or on sequences starting with other tokens (apart from a single a-y case).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 22 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=y (+3.48), next_out=r (+1.64), prev_tok=w (+1.62), orig1=r (+1.56), t=7 & prev_tok=x (+1.45), phase=1 & out_tok=r (+1.36). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.00), in_count=1 (-1.53), orig5=- (-1.46), L=9 (-1.20).
